sources.title: Associates Program Operating Agreement
sources.supports: Section 1 defines Special Links as links that 'must properly use the special tagged link formats we provide'. Section 5 requires the exact sentence used in the disclosure bar on every page.
sources.quote: You must clearly and prominently state the following ... on your Site ...: "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases."

sources.title: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements
sources.supports: 2(b): the Associates ID must appear as a URL parameter in every link to an Amazon Site, and all Special Links must be accessed directly from the site. 2(b) also restricts price and availability display to Amazon-served data or the Creators/PA API. 6(t) restricts customer reviews and star ratings to API-supplied data. 6(u) bars buying through your own links. 6(v) bars cloaking or Redirecting Links. 6(w) bars link shortening that obscures the Amazon destination. 6(y) bars price tracking.
sources.quote: All Special Links must be accessed directly from your Site. ... you must include your Associates ID or "tag" ... as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site.

sources.title: Associates Program Commission Income Statement
sources.method: full (section of the Program Policies page)
sources.supports: How a click becomes a qualifying purchase: a session lasts 24 hours from the click, or up to 89 days if the item is added to the cart first. Section 2(g) disqualifies purchases that are 'not correctly tracked or reported because the links from your site' are not properly formatted — the policy reason this edition tests link formatting before scaling.
sources.quote: during a single session, which is measured as beginning when a customer clicks through that Special Link and ending upon the first to occur of the following: (x) 24 hours elapse from that click

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links to Google
sources.supports: The rel="sponsored" attribute applied to every Amazon link on this site.
sources.quote: Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links) with the sponsored value.

sources.title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking — the affiliate-marketing section
sources.supports: Supplies the first sentence of the disclosure bar verbatim as the FTC's own example for affiliate links, and says the disclosure belongs close to the recommendation. Also states that 'affiliate link' alone and a 'buy now' button are not adequate, while 'paid link' next to the link can be.
sources.quote: You could say something like, "I get commissions for purchases made through links in this post."

sources.title: 16 CFR 255.5 — Disclosure of material connections
sources.supports: The legal rule behind the disclosure bar: a material connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously, in a way a reader can evaluate.
sources.quote: such connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously

sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service
sources.supports: Every temperature in the thermometer guide, row by row: 145 °F with a 3-minute rest for steaks, chops and roasts; 160 °F ground meats and eggs; 165 °F ground poultry, all poultry, leftovers and casseroles; 145 °F fish and shellfish.
sources.quote: Ground Meats | 160 degrees F (71.1 degrees C)

sources.title: Food Thermometers
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service
sources.supports: Where to place a probe (whole poultry: thigh, wing, thickest breast, avoiding bone), the 2–4 °F accuracy expectation for consumer thermometers, and that a thermometer should not be left in food unless the manufacturer says it is built for that.
sources.quote: Most food thermometers will give an accurate reading within 2 to 4 degrees F

sources.title: Understanding ASINs
sources.supports: The Amazon-owned definition that earlier sessions recorded as unfindable: an ASIN is a 10-character alphanumeric code and appears after /dp/ in a product URL. This is why a 9-character supplied token is recorded as a format mismatch rather than read as an ASIN.
sources.quote: It's a unique 10-character alphanumeric code assigned to every product listed in the Amazon store.
